# Frozen CEMB compatibility corpus

These eight binary fixtures are native encoder output from three historical
revisions. Positive compatibility tests never relabel a current-format body.

| Wire version | Historical producer revision | Cases |
| ------------ | ---------------------------- | ----- |
| 2 | `75fe1fa664cc30e57a8b42fe057c110060b608f9` | literal attribute, ordinary subtree |
| 3 | `4ba5a9ff626c55de8fac506040cbdea0c33cffb4` | literal attribute, pending reference, cyclic/duplicate reference targets |
| 4 | `1d44d28284234e9a74bb80b97aab897bf85c9f97` | literal attribute, pending reference, cyclic/duplicate reference targets |

The `.cem` inputs are exact UTF-8 bytes without an appended newline, matching the
original regressions. `produce.rs` parses them with `SourceId(1)`, sets the
explicit non-owning target lists for the graph case, and invokes the historical
encoder unchanged. That revision's decoder must accept its own output before
the fixture is saved. `*.expected.json` contains explicitly named, test-only
observations of canonical source, node count, attributes and references recorded
from the historical document before encoding. These are independent expectations
for the current decoder, including every original source-map frame.

`provenance.json` records producer revisions, encoder/format/Cargo-lock hashes,
the shared driver hash, and byte counts/SHA-256 for each binary, source and
observation file. The current [test helper](../../support/legacy_cemb.rs) checks
these fixture hashes and exact decoded observations. Tests also require empty
native value slots on legacy literal attributes, original ID binding, pending
versus empty target states, duplicate/self/cyclic non-owning edges, retained-owner
identity and complete current-v5 source-map round trips.

Older source stacks legitimately predate additional expression-embedding frames.
They must match their own frozen producer observations exactly. Adding modern
frames to historical sources would alter their provenance.

Normal Cargo tests read these files directly and require no historical checkout,
Git invocation or network access. To deliberately regenerate the corpus from the
repository root with the pinned Rust 1.96.0 toolchain:

```sh
python3 packages/cem_ml/tests/fixtures/cemb-legacy/regenerate.py
```

The script archives each pinned revision into its own temporary directory and
uses an independent Cargo target directory per producer. It copies only the
shared example driver into those archives; historical parser, formatter,
encoder/decoder, lockfile and package sources remain unchanged. It removes the
temporary checkouts and build outputs after generation. The locked dependency
builds may download missing crates. Review regenerated bytes and provenance as a
fixture update rather than accepting a current encoder's changed header.

Header relabeling remains intentional only for negative cases: reference tags
under a v2 header, or current metadata presented as an older wire format. Corrupt
hashes, re-sealed structural truncation and zero-count limits must also refuse.
